findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-verify the 'no public InstrumentedModel' claim against pydantic-ai 1.107.2 (it resolves in-env and is documented) and either correct it or explicitly justify why InstrumentedModel/WrapperModel cannot be reused for the per-candidate spans before committing to a parallel-tracer wrapper.
evidence: resolve_symbol: pydantic_ai.models.instrumented.InstrumentedModel EXISTS (site-packages origin) — contradicting the plan's 'no public InstrumentedModel' claim
resolve_symbol: pydantic_ai.models.wrapper.WrapperModel and pydantic_ai.models.instrumented.InstrumentationSettings both EXIST in the installed environment

Retrieved Pydantic AI docs (ai.pydantic.dev/api/models/instrumented): 'class InstrumentedModel(WrapperModel): Model which wraps another model so that requests are instrumented with OpenTelemetry' — a documented public wrapping facility
Plan crosses a bright-line: it introduces a novel per-candidate span-emitting wrapper on the raw OTel tracer, a parallel instrumentation system
findings.finding: The Approach's load-bearing capability assertion — 'pydantic-ai 1.107.2 exposes no public InstrumentedModel' — appears to be incorrect: pydantic_ai.models.instrumented.InstrumentedModel (a WrapperModel subclass) resolves in the installed environment and is publicly documented as the library's own 'model which wraps another model so that requests are instrumented with OpenTelemetry.' Because this claim is used to justify building a parallel bespoke tracer wrapper instead of reusing the library facility, the novel architecture is chosen without weighing the most directly relevant prior art (InstrumentedModel / WrapperModel).
findings.location: Approach — 'pydantic-ai 1.107.2 exposes no public InstrumentedModel, so we reuse the same OTel tracer rather than a parallel system'
scenarios: Wrapping each concrete FallbackModel candidate to emit candidate child spans (Mechanism A) — the exact use case InstrumentedModel/WrapperModel address
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the installed pydantic-ai version and re-check pydantic_ai.models.instrumented.InstrumentedModel / pydantic_ai.models.wrapper.WrapperModel. If present, either adopt WrapperModel/InstrumentedModel to instrument each candidate (aligning with the library's OTel GenAI conventions), or record a concrete reason it is unsuitable (e.g. it emits a full model-request span per candidate rather than a nested child span under the logical turn) so the novel parallel-tracer design is justified against the real prior art rather than an unverified absence claim.

evidence: Prerequisite: 'Replace the manual attempt scheduler with one Pydantic Agent run composing the S1 adapter' and 'Invalid-then-valid output completes in one Agent run reporting exactly two requests under one shared UsageLimits'

Prerequisite NativeOutput note: 'the NativeOutput branch runs as the same bounded operation ... sharing the wire projection and the one output-retry counter' with the 895c fallback to prompted path kept within one operation

Subject: '_pai_structured ... performs TWO separate agent.run_sync calls (native attempt, then on a schema-complexity rejection a prompted attempt) and therefore is two distinct Agent-request turns by design'
Subject AC: 'Native-to-prompted downgrade emits two distinct Agent-request turns ... adding the second Agent run by design'
findings.finding: The prerequisite S2 replaces the manual `_pai_structured` attempt scheduler with ONE bounded Agent operation composing the S1 adapter, explicitly eliminating any separate output-recovery Agent run so that invalid-then-valid output completes in one Agent run. The subject plan (S4) contradicts this by describing Mechanism B (native-to-prompted downgrade) in `_pai_structured` as performing TWO separate `agent.run_sync` calls that are 'two distinct Agent-request turns by design,' and its acceptance criteria assert the downgrade 'emits two distinct Agent-request turns' and 'adds the second Agent run by design.' The prerequisite consolidates output recovery (including the native-to-prompted path) into a single Agent operation, while the subject treats the native/prompted transition as two separate Agent runs, conflicting on the fundamental control-flow shape of `_pai_structured`.
scenarios: 895c grammar-compilation fallback from native to prompted path
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile the Mechanism B model: if S2's single-operation `_pai_structured` lands first, the subject should instrument the native-to-prompted transition as attempts/turns within one Agent operation rather than as two distinct Agent runs, or explicitly stage the subject after/against the pre-S2 two-run implementation.

Testing only asserts 'Tracing disabled: identical result, usage, imports, and exception behavior' — no symmetric assertion for tracing ENABLED that a span/exporter error is isolated from the real control flow

findings.finding: The plan guarantees identical exception behavior only with tracing DISABLED; it does not state that a span-emission/exporter failure while tracing is ENABLED must not perturb the real fallback result or mask/alter the underlying provider exception.
findings.location: Approach / Testing 'Tracing disabled: identical ... exception behavior' / Acceptance Criteria

Span code throws and the FallbackExceptionGroup ordering or resolution classification changes when tracing is on
findings.suggested_fix: State that candidate/turn instrumentation wraps span operations so that any exception from span recording or the exporter is caught and does not propagate into the fallback control flow, and add a test injecting an exporter/span-recording failure to prove the real result and exception are unchanged.
